Climbing route through the channel

Through one leg and load rib
Full route shown while paused
Solid sectionIllustrative surface route

Overhanging route: tray underside → sloped channel wall → crown underside. The 360° channel is retained. The closed lower membrane and a sealed crown seating joint prevent an interior shortcut through the open deck.

Before printing and use

Six legs with a clear inverted underside

Six Ø32 / Ø14 mm legs sit on a Ø126 mm circle. The 16.1° taper is retained. Roots and buried beam ends stop before the outer underside; a smooth continuous seating rib at radii 77–80 mm supports the crown. The outer 10 mm underside remains clear around the full perimeter, restoring the inverted traversal before reaching the side channel. Minimum support radius is 61.2 mm versus 56.1 mm for the physically printed four-leg base. Insetting the feet reduces it from the previous eight-leg design's 74.0 mm. These are geometry comparisons, not physical tip ratings. The 1.2 mm panel, six deep beams and original mating geometry remain.

Liquid or tape placement

Two integral 2 mm rims contain a channel 7.4 mm wide at its floor; a 1 mm liquid depth holds about 3.85 mL. The floor is 1.2 mm thick. The inner wall flares outward by 4 mm at 21.8° from vertical. The locating rim follows its slope with assembly clearance. Thin tape can line the cap underside. Follow the liquid product label and test for leaks with water first.

Legs up, supports OFF

The new base has six connected legs and no outboard caps or exposed beam ends. Preserve the supplied orientations on two plates: base legs up, crown contact face on the bed. Its roots grow from the closed central panel; the annular seating rib grows from the channel floor. The base is checked with A1 / Generic PLA / 0.2 mm Standard / supports OFF; unchanged crown and sample records are reused by matching STL hashes. The 6.6 mm channel bridge still needs a physical print check. Clean and dry the cooled plate before starting. The open crown lattice is intentional; missing lines on designed solid surfaces are defects.

Seal the continuous seating joint

Dry-fit the crown, then fully seat it with a thin, continuous bonded seal around its bottom ring (radius 79.2–80 mm). A dry-fit gap can let ants enter the hollow crown and reach the open top. Keep sealant inside the locating rim and preserve the side channel. The liquid trough itself belongs entirely to the base.

The power cord can bypass the barrier

This stand addresses the route from the table through the legs. The power cord reaches the kettle base directly and needs separate ant isolation. Keep cords, walls and other objects from bridging the channel.

For the original plastic power base

The kettle holds 1.7 L. Its base diameter, full operating weight and contact temperature have not been measured. Keep it centered, seat protruding rubber feet on deep beams or ring/beam junctions, and preserve ventilation and cable clearance. Ring radii are editable if the feet land in openings. Tapered legs and inverted surfaces alone do not guarantee ant exclusion.
